name: Florida Power & Light (FPL)
rate_note: All-in energy rate = base energy + conservation + capacity + environmental + storm protection + fuel + transition credit, as printed in FPL's 'Residential Rates and Clauses' insert effective October 2026 (cents/kWh: base 7.865 / 8.865, conservation 0.148, capacity 0.052, environmental 0.345, storm protection 0.995, fuel 2.893 / 3.893, transition credit -0.040 for up to / over 1,000 kWh). Taxes, franchise fees and gross receipts taxes are not included. FPL applies a $30 minimum base bill.

name: Duke Energy Florida
rate_note: Duke's RS-1 base energy charge is seasonal: 'tiers' is the Summer rate (March to November), 'winter_tiers' is the Winter rate (December to February). All-in rate = base energy + fuel + conservation + capacity + environmental + asset securitization + storm protection plan surcharge (+ storm cost recovery surcharge, which is zero), from Duke's 'Base Rates by Rate Schedule' and 'Clause Rates by Rate Schedule' tables effective October 2026 (cents/kWh, up to / over 1,000 kWh: summer base 7.731 / 8.503, winter base 8.805 / 10.302, fuel 4.127 / 5.197, conservation 0.386, capacity 0.133, environmental 0.040, asset securitization 0.238, storm protection plan 0.936). Taxes and franchise fees are not included. Duke applies a $30 minimum bill.
fixed_charge_note: RS-1 customer charge, secondary voltage, per month.

name: Tampa Electric (TECO)
rate_note: All-in rate = energy charge + fuel charge + storm protection charge + clean energy transition mechanism, from Tampa Electric's 'Approved Rates for January 2026' insert (cents/kWh, up to / over 1,000 kWh: energy 9.569 / 10.569, fuel 3.210 / 4.210, storm protection 0.717, clean energy transition 0.406). The energy charge already includes conservation, environmental and capacity recovery. The temporary storm surcharge (1.995 cents/kWh) is excluded because the insert says it ends in August 2026. The insert is dated January 2026, so fuel or other charges may have changed since. Taxes and franchise fees are not included.
fixed_charge_note: Basic service charge is published as 0.45 cents per day; the monthly figure converts it as 0.0045 x 365 / 12 (rounded to cents).

name: Pacific Gas and Electric (PG&E)

tou_rates.label: Summer peak (4-9 p.m. every day), total usage
Winter peak (4-9 p.m. every day), total usage

tou_note: Total bundled rates from the E-TOU-C tariff sheet effective June 1, 2026. A baseline credit applies to baseline usage only. PG&E publishes no blended average for this plan, so avg_rate_per_kwh is null rather than computed from an assumed usage split. PG&E's residential rate plan pricing sheet (pge.com/assets/pge/docs/account/rate-plans/residential-electric-rate-plan-pricing.pdf) defines Summer as June 1 to Sept 30 and Winter as Oct 1 to May 31. Customers served by a community choice provider (e.g. CleanPowerSF, Peninsula Clean Energy) pay different generation rates.
fixed_charge_note: Base Services Charge is published per day by income tier ($0.19713 Tier 1, $0.39688 Tier 2, $0.79343 Tier 3). The monthly figure is Tier 3 (customers not on CARE or FERA, the default) converted as 0.79343 x 365 / 12 (rounded to cents).

name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
tou_note: Prices as shown on SCE's Time-of-Use Residential Rate Plans page for 'TOU-D 4 PM to 9 PM', before the baseline credit and rounded to the nearest cent by SCE. The page is undated and SCE announced a residential rate change effective October 1, 2026, so these may lag the current tariff. SCE publishes no blended average for this plan, so avg_rate_per_kwh is null rather than computed from an assumed usage split.
fixed_charge_note: Base Services Charge is published as $0.79 per day; the monthly figure converts it as 0.79 x 365 / 12 (rounded to cents).

name: San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E)
tou_note: Total electric rates (bundled service with SDG&E generation) from the TOU-DR1 total rates table effective August 1, 2026; the table does not state the season dates. The 'up to 130% of baseline' adjustment credit applies to the first usage each month. SDG&E publishes no blended average for this plan, so avg_rate_per_kwh is null rather than computed from an assumed usage split. Customers on San Diego Community Power or Clean Energy Alliance pay different generation rates.
fixed_charge_note: Base Services Charge is published as $0.79343 per day (standard TOU-DR1 customer); the monthly figure converts it as 0.79343 x 365 / 12 (rounded to cents).
